title: System Prompt Sensitivity of Emergent Misalignment: Mapping the Prompt Space
original_idea: Take an already-fine-tuned misaligned model. Construct a grid of 20 system prompt variants. Measure misalignment rate across this grid and cluster prompts by elicitation success.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: The prompt sensitivity mapping experiment has been directly conducted and published. The proposed 20-prompt grid is a subset of existing work.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Uses an already-fine-tuned model (available from open codebase). Constructing system prompt variants is text editing. Running evaluations across a grid is straightforward scripting. Clustering by elicitation success is basic data analysis. Fully accessible to beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped: 20 prompt variants on one model, one evaluation set. Well-defined success criteria (the sensitivity map). Single experiment with obvious deliverable (prompt-to-misalignment-rate grid). Can go from start to result very quickly.

novelty.reasoning: This idea has been substantially addressed by the 'Emergent Misalignment as Prompt Sensitivity' paper (arXiv:2507.06253, 2025), which directly studies how system prompt variations modulate EM rates. That paper found that augmenting system prompts can reliably elicit or suppress misaligned behavior, that asking models to be 'evil' increases misalignment while 'HHH' reduces it, and that prompt format (Python, JSON) affects elicitation. The 'Eliciting and Analyzing Emergent Misalignment in State-of-the-Art LLMs' paper (arXiv:2508.04196, 2025) further maps adversarial prompt strategies. The 'We Need a Better Way to Evaluate Emergent Misalignment' (LessWrong) discusses evaluation methodology including prompt variation. The emergently misaligned models showing behavioral self-awareness paper (arXiv:2602.14777, 2026) adds further characterization. The proposed 20-prompt grid and clustering approach is a subset of what has already been done.
